indian_entity: Early Ayurvedic formulary tradition (Navanitaka; Caraka/Susruta/Bhela-line material)
chinese_source: EXTERNAL physical anchor (non-Chinese record): birch-bark manuscript in Gupta script, excavated from a stupa near Kucha (Xinjiang), now Bodleian MS Sansk. c.17
event: Three of the Bower Manuscript's seven treatises are medical; the Navanitaka formulary opens with a recipe that also stands in the Caraka Samhita and excerpts Caraka-, Susruta- and Bhela-line material
date_raw: Palaeographic dating (Gupta script; letter ya forms); no radiocarbon published
firmness_reason: Palaeographic range (Sander 500-550; Callewaert c. 450; Hoernle's final view 4th-5th c.); a published radiocarbon date would make it firm
notes: A TAQ for the formulary SYSTEM behind the samhitas, not for any one samhita's final form: by c. 500 the eight-branch corpus was mature and excerptable on the Silk Road.
